claims.boundary: Two transition models on the same three fully observed physical states START/LEFT/RIGHT, with two actions TEST/RANDOM and no reset in the scored interaction. TEST at START selects the absorbing state named by the model; RANDOM selects either terminal state fairly and independently of the model; all later actions self-loop. The literal normalized discounted state occupancy is (1-gamma) times the infinite sum of gamma^t times the actual policy-induced physical-state marginal, including the fixed initial state. The objective is entropy after averaging occupancy, evaluated separately in each fixed MDP, with no prior mixture inside entropy. For every 0<gamma<1 and arbitrary valid randomized history policy, the exact score is h(gamma)+gamma*h((1+p)/2), where p is initial TEST probability. All and only p=0 policies maximize, with attained finite maximum h(gamma)+gamma*log(2). Every optimizer has class-independent full records and exact deficiency 1/2 to the actual one-step TEST experiment at every finite time, hence eventual deficiency 1/2. TEST reveals the model and is finitarily greatest, strictly dominating every optimizer. Any family of exact optimizers retains deficiency 1/2, including as proper discounts tend to one; no limiting-policy convergence assumption. This is the published state-distribution entropy objective, not empirical raw-label entropy or a claim about the source learning algorithm and its reset-based training guarantee. Selected-manuscript integration on 26 September also defines the infimum of these original per-world values over the two worlds. IntrinsicWorstCaseSelection proves attainment and the stated native-deficiency conclusions for every optimizer of this scalar objective; DIAYN retains its entire [1/4,1/2] range. Original per-world results remain in scope.
